subproblem.title: C¹ radial cutoffs whose integrals converge to the mass of the open ball
subproblem.statement: There is a sequence of functions η_j : ℝ → ℝ (j ∈ ℕ) such that every η_j is C¹, η_j ≥ 0, deriv η_j ≤ 0 everywhere, and η_j(u) = 0 for u ≥ 1, and such that for every P ∈ ℕ, every measure μ on ℝ^P, every z ∈ ℝ^P and every s > 0 with μ(B_s(z)) < ∞ (open ball): ∫ η_j(|x − z|²/s²) dμ(x) → μ(B_s(z)) (as a real number, μ.real (ball z s)) as j → ∞.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∃ η : ℕ → ℝ → ℝ, (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ 1 (η j)) ∧ (∀ j u, 0 ≤ η j u) ∧ (∀ j u, deriv (η j) u ≤ 0) ∧ (∀ j u, 1 ≤ u → η j u = 0) ∧ ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (z : Euclid P) (s : ℝ), 0 < s → μ (ball z s) < ∞ → Tendsto (fun j => ∫ x, η j (‖x - z‖ ^ 2 / s ^ 2) ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (μ.real (ball z s)))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 6(a)–(c) of the parent proof. These are the cutoffs g((1 − t)/ε_j) with ε_j = 1/(j + 2) and g = Mathlib's Real.smoothTransition, which the parent proof explicitly allows. Here they are applied to the squared radius ratio u = |x − z|²/s². Open balls appear because the cutoffs increase to the indicator of (−∞, 1).
1. Definition. Let g := Real.smoothTransition. It is C^∞ and monotone, satisfies 0 ≤ g ≤ 1, g(t) = 0 for t ≤ 0 and g(t) = 1 for t ≥ 1. Put η_j(u) := g((j + 2)·(1 − u)).
2. C¹. η_j is the composition of the C^∞ function g with the affine map u ↦ (j + 2)(1 − u), hence C¹.
3. Nonnegativity: η_j ≥ 0 because g ≥ 0.
4. Sign of the derivative. Since j + 2 > 0, u ↦ (j + 2)(1 − u) is antitone; g is monotone, so η_j is antitone. The derivative of an antitone function ℝ → ℝ is ≤ 0 at every point (Antitone.deriv_nonpos), so deriv η_j ≤ 0 everywhere.
5. Vanishing. If u ≥ 1, then (j + 2)(1 − u) ≤ 0, so η_j(u) = g((j + 2)(1 − u)) = 0.
6. Convergence. Fix P, μ, z and s > 0 with μ(B_s(z)) < ∞, and put u(x) := |x − z|²/s².
 (a) Domination. 0 ≤ η_j(u(x)) ≤ 1 for all x, and if x ∉ B_s(z) then u(x) ≥ 1 (because |x − z| ≥ s > 0), so η_j(u(x)) = 0 by step 5. Hence |η_j(u(x))| ≤ 1_{B_s(z)}(x) for all j and x, and 1_{B_s(z)} is μ-integrable because μ(B_s(z)) < ∞. Each x ↦ η_j(u(x)) is continuous, hence AEStronglyMeasurable.
 (b) Pointwise limit. If x ∈ B_s(z), then u(x) < 1. Choose N ∈ ℕ with N ≥ 1/(1 − u(x)). For j ≥ N, (j + 2)(1 − u(x)) ≥ 1, so η_j(u(x)) = 1. Thus η_j(u(x)) → 1 = 1_{B_s(z)}(x). If x ∉ B_s(z), then η_j(u(x)) = 0 = 1_{B_s(z)}(x) for every j.
 (c) By dominated convergence (tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence) with the bound 1_{B_s(z)}, ∫ η_j(u) dμ → ∫ 1_{B_s(z)} dμ = μ.real(B_s(z)) (integral_indicator_one).
Lean remark (optional aid; the proof above is complete without it): during decomposition, a warning-free, kernel-checked proof of exactly this frozen type was written. It uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and it follows steps 1–6. Scratch copies, which may no longer exist: /tmp/dsmc-em-decomp/C4.lean, and /tmp/dsmc-em-decomp/Full.lean (all four children plus the parent assembly).
proof_key_steps: η_j(u) := Real.smoothTransition((j + 2)(1 − u)) is C¹, nonnegative, antitone (so deriv ≤ 0), and vanishes for u ≥ 1.
For s > 0, 0 ≤ η_j(|x − z|²/s²) ≤ 1_{B_s(z)}(x), integrable since μ(B_s(z)) < ∞.
η_j(|x − z|²/s²) → 1_{B_s(z)}(x) for every x: eventually (j + 2)(1 − u) ≥ 1 when u < 1, and the value is 0 when u ≥ 1.
Dominated convergence gives ∫η_j(|x − z|²/s²) dμ → ∫1_{B_s(z)} dμ = μ.real(B_s(z)).

audit.reason: The explicit smoothTransition family satisfies every quantified property. Its radial values are zero on the sphere and exterior and eventually one at each interior point. Domination by the integrable open-ball indicator proves precisely convergence to μ.real (ball z s). The construction is universal, complete, and non-circular.

subproblem.title: Radial first-variation inequality n∫η(u_s) + ∫2u_sη′(u_s) ≤ κs∫η(u_s) under bounded mean curvature (Simon Ch. 4, 3.2–3.3, 3.14–3.16)
subproblem.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P, R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep U n with μ := μ_R = θHⁿ⌞M (R.measure), H : ℝ^P → ℝ^P, κ, r ∈ ℝ, z ∈ ℝ^P and η : ℝ → ℝ. Assume: B̄_r(z) ⊆ U; x ↦ p_x, the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x, is μ-AEMeasurable; |H(x)| ≤ κ for all x; R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ for every C¹ vector field X with compact support and tsupport X ⊆ B_r(z); η is C¹, η ≥ 0, deriv η ≤ 0 everywhere, and η(u) = 0 for u ≥ 1. Then for every s with 0 < s < r, writing u_s(x) := |x − z|²/s² and η′ := deriv η: n·∫η(u_s) dμ + ∫ 2·u_s·η′(u_s) dμ ≤ κ·s·∫η(u_s) dμ. (Measurability of H is not needed.)
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n) (H : Euclid P → Euclid P) (κ : ℝ) (z : Euclid P) (r : ℝ) (η : ℝ → ℝ), closedBall z r ⊆ U → AEMeasurable (fun x => (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection) R.measure → (∀ x, ‖H x‖ ≤ κ) → (∀ X : Euclid P → Euclid P, ContDiff ℝ 1 X → HasCompactSupport X → tsupport X ⊆ ball z r → R.firstVariation X = -∫ x, inner ℝ (X x) (H x) ∂R.measure) → ContDiff ℝ 1 η → (∀ u, 0 ≤ η u) → (∀ u, deriv η u ≤ 0) → (∀ u, 1 ≤ u → η u = 0) → ∀ s : ℝ, 0 < s → s < r → (n : ℝ) * ∫ x, η (‖x - z‖ ^ 2 / s ^ 2) ∂R.measure + ∫ x, 2 * (‖x - z‖ ^ 2 / s ^ 2) * deriv η (‖x - z‖ ^ 2 / s ^ 2) ∂R.measure ≤ κ * s * ∫ x, η (‖x - z‖ ^ 2 / s ^ 2) ∂R.measure
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: steps 0(a)–(c), 2 and 3 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, 3.1–3.3 with the bounded generalized mean curvature of 3.14–3.16; sign convention δV(X) = −∫X·H). The radial field is written with the squared radius ratio: X(x) = η(|x − z|²/s²)(x − z) is the parent's φ_s(x)(x − z) with γ(τ) = η(τ²) for τ ≥ 0 (only τ = ϱ/s ≥ 0 occurs). Then the parent's ψ_s = (ϱ/s)γ′(ϱ/s) equals 2u_sη′(u_s), the identity div_M X = nφ_s + ψ_s q becomes step 3 below, and (★) becomes the claim. Steps 5–6 prove inline the special case of the sibling first_variation_integral (Submission.dsmc_firstVariation_eq_integral) that the parent proof cites in step 3(a). This child therefore has no dependencies.
Fix s with 0 < s < r. Write μ := R.measure, M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult, u(x) := u_s(x) = |x − z|²/s² ≥ 0 and η′ := deriv η.
0. Preliminaries.
 (a) κ ≥ 0, because 0 ≤ |H(0)| ≤ κ.
 (b) μ(B̄_r(z)) < ∞. The closed ball B̄_r(z) is compact, measurable and contained in U, and μ(B̄_r(z)) = ∫⁻_{M ∩ B̄_r(z)} θ dHⁿ (withDensity_apply, Measure.restrict_restrict). This is ≠ ∞ by R.locallyIntegrable_mult. Hence μ(B_r(z)) < ∞, and c·1_{B_r(z)} is μ-integrable for every constant c.
 (c) η′ is continuous and η′(u) = 0 for u ≥ 1. For u > 1, η vanishes on the neighbourhood (1, ∞) of u, and η′(1) = 0 follows by continuity of η′. Choose C, M₀ ≥ 0 with |η| ≤ C and |η′| ≤ M₀ on [0, 1] (compactness). If x ∉ B_s(z), then u(x) ≥ 1, so η(u(x)) = η′(u(x)) = 0. If x ∈ B_s(z), then 0 ≤ u(x) ≤ 1. In particular, η(u(x)) ≠ 0 implies |x − z| < s.
 (d) The functions x ↦ η(u(x)) and x ↦ 2u(x)η′(u(x)) are continuous, are bounded by C·1_{B_r(z)} and 2M₀·1_{B_r(z)} respectively (by (c), since B_s(z) ⊆ B_r(z)), and are therefore μ-integrable by (b).
1. The radial field. Let X(x) := η(u(x))·(x − z). As a product of C¹ maps, X is C¹; no case distinction at x = z is needed, because u is a polynomial in x. Since Du(x)v = (2/s²)⟨x − z, v⟩, the product and chain rules give DX(x)v = η(u(x))·v + η′(u(x))·(2/s²)·⟨x − z, v⟩·(x − z). By (c), X(x) = 0 for x ∉ B_s(z). So tsupport X ⊆ B̄_s(z), X has compact support, and tsupport X ⊆ B̄_s(z) ⊆ B_r(z) because s < r. The hypothesis therefore applies: R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ.
2. Orthonormal frames a.e. By R.orients, for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q. The latter gives an orthonormal family τ = (τ₁, …, τₙ) with span{τᵢ} = Q. For such x, approxTangentPlane n M x = Q. Indeed, by definition approxTangentPlane n M x is a chosen Q′ with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q′, and approximate tangent spaces are unique (HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique). Hence p_x = Σᵢ τᵢ⟨τᵢ, ·⟩: expand the orthogonal projection onto span{τᵢ} in the orthonormal basis τ (OrthonormalBasis.starProjection_eq_sum_rankOne). Because μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous), this representation holds for μ-a.e. x.
3. The divergence. Let x be as in step 2. The trace of τ⟨τ, ·⟩ ∘ L is ⟨τ, Lτ⟩, so div_M X(x) = trace(p_x ∘ DX(x)) = Σᵢ ⟨τᵢ, DX(x)τᵢ⟩. Using |τᵢ| = 1, this equals Σᵢ [η(u(x)) + η′(u(x))(2/s²)⟨x − z, τᵢ⟩²] = n·η(u(x)) + η′(u(x))·(2/s²)·Σᵢ⟨τᵢ, x − z⟩².
4. Two-sided bound. By Bessel's inequality, 0 ≤ Σᵢ⟨τᵢ, x − z⟩² ≤ |x − z|². The coefficient η′(u(x))·(2/s²) is ≤ 0, and (2/s²)|x − z|² = 2u(x). Hence for μ-a.e. x:
 n·η(u(x)) + 2u(x)·η′(u(x)) ≤ div_M X(x) ≤ n·η(u(x)).
5. Integrability of div_M X.
 Measurability: x ↦ p_x is μ-AEMeasurable by hypothesis, with values in the finite-dimensional normed space L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P), so it is AEStronglyMeasurable. x ↦ DX(x) is continuous because X is C¹. The map (A, B) ↦ trace(A ∘ B) is continuous on L(ℝ^P, ℝ^P)², so div_M X = trace(p_x ∘ DX(x)) is AEStronglyMeasurable.
 Bound: for μ-a.e. x ∈ B_s(z), step 4 together with u(x) ≤ 1, |η| ≤ C and |η′| ≤ M₀ gives |div_M X(x)| ≤ n·C + 2M₀. For μ-a.e. x ∉ B_s(z), both bounds in step 4 vanish because η(u(x)) = η′(u(x)) = 0, so div_M X(x) = 0. Thus |div_M X| ≤ (nC + 2M₀)·1_{B_r(z)} μ-a.e., which is integrable by 0(b).
6. First variation as a μ-integral. For every f : ℝ^P → ℝ, ∫ f dμ = ∫_M θ·f dHⁿ. This is integral_withDensity_eq_integral_smul with the measurable ℝ≥0-valued density θ, and it holds without any integrability assumption on f. With f = div_M X it gives ∫ div_M X dμ = R.firstVariation X.
7. Lower bound. By 0(d), ∫(nη(u) + 2uη′(u)) dμ = n∫η(u) dμ + ∫2uη′(u) dμ. By step 4, step 5 and integral_mono_ae, followed by steps 6 and 1:
 n∫η(u) dμ + ∫2uη′(u) dμ ≤ ∫ div_M X dμ = R.firstVariation X = −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ.
8. Mean curvature term. −∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ ≤ |∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ| ≤ ∫|⟨X, H⟩| dμ (norm_integral_le_integral_norm, valid even if ⟨X, H⟩ is not integrable). Pointwise, if η(u(x)) = 0 then X(x) = 0. Otherwise |x − z| < s by 0(c), and since η ≥ 0 and κ ≥ 0, |⟨X(x), H(x)⟩| ≤ |X(x)|·|H(x)| ≤ η(u(x))·|x − z|·κ ≤ κ·s·η(u(x)). As |⟨X, H⟩| ≥ 0 and κ·s·η(u) is integrable (0(d)), integral_mono_of_nonneg gives ∫|⟨X, H⟩| dμ ≤ κ·s·∫η(u) dμ. No measurability of H is used.
9. Combining steps 7 and 8: n·∫η(u_s) dμ + ∫2u_sη′(u_s) dμ ≤ κ·s·∫η(u_s) dμ.

X = η(|x − z|²/s²)(x − z) is C¹ with tsupport in B̄_s(z) ⊆ B_r(z), and DX(x)v = η(u)v + η′(u)(2/s²)⟨x − z, v⟩(x − z).
For μ-a.e. x, R.orients and uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces give p_x = Σᵢτᵢ⟨τᵢ, ·⟩ with τ orthonormal of size n, so div_M X = nη(u) + η′(u)(2/s²)Σᵢ⟨τᵢ, x − z⟩².
Bessel and η′ ≤ 0 give nη(u) + 2uη′(u) ≤ div_M X ≤ nη(u) a.e., so div_M X is integrable; integrate and use ∫div_M X dμ = R.firstVariation X (withDensity).
−∫⟨X, H⟩ dμ ≤ ∫|⟨X, H⟩| dμ ≤ κs∫η(u) dμ, because |X| ≤ η(u)·s where η(u) ≠ 0.

subproblem.title: Continuity and differentiability of radial cutoff integrals I(t) = ∫ η(|x − z|²/t²) dμ
subproblem.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, let μ be a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra of Euclid P), z ∈ ℝ^P and r ∈ ℝ with μ(B_r(z)) < ∞ (open ball). Let η : ℝ → ℝ be C¹ with η(u) = 0 for all u ≥ 1, and put I(t) := ∫ η(|x − z|²/t²) dμ(x) (Bochner integral). Then (i) I is continuous on (0, r]; (ii) for every s ∈ (0, r), I has derivative −(1/s)·∫ 2·(|x − z|²/s²)·η′(|x − z|²/s²) dμ(x) at s, where η′ = deriv η (written −(∫ 2·(‖x − z‖²/s²)·deriv η (‖x − z‖²/s²) dμ)/s).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (z : Euclid P) (r : ℝ) (η : ℝ → ℝ), μ (ball z r) < ∞ → ContDiff ℝ 1 η → (∀ u, 1 ≤ u → η u = 0) → ContinuousOn (fun t => ∫ x, η (‖x - z‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 2) ∂μ) (Ioc 0 r) ∧ ∀ s ∈ Ioo 0 r, HasDerivAt (fun t => ∫ x, η (‖x - z‖ ^ 2 / t ^ 2) ∂μ) (-(∫ x, 2 * (‖x - z‖ ^ 2 / s ^ 2) * deriv η (‖x - z‖ ^ 2 / s ^ 2) ∂μ) / s) s
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof: differentiation of I under the integral sign, and continuity of I on (0, r] by dominated convergence. Here the cutoff is written in the squared radius ratio, φ_t(x) = η(|x − z|²/t²); this is the parent's γ(ϱ/t) with γ(τ) = η(τ²) for τ ≥ 0 (only τ = ϱ/t ≥ 0 occurs).
Notation: u_t(x) := |x − z|²/t² ≥ 0 and η′ := deriv η. If r ≤ 0, then (0, r] and (0, r) are empty and both conclusions are vacuous; the argument below covers this case.
1. η′ is continuous, since η is C¹. Moreover η′(u) = 0 for every u ≥ 1. For u > 1, η vanishes on the neighbourhood (1, ∞) of u, so η′(u) = 0. Then η′(1) = 0, because η′ is continuous at 1 and equals 0 on (1, ∞) (uniqueness of limits along 𝓝[>] 1).
2. Bounds. Since [0, 1] is compact and η, η′ are continuous, there are C, M ≥ 0 with |η(u)| ≤ C and |η′(u)| ≤ M for all u ∈ [0, 1].
3. Support. Let t > 0. If |x − z| ≥ t, then u_t(x) ≥ 1, so η(u_t(x)) = 0 and η′(u_t(x)) = 0. If |x − z| < t, then 0 ≤ u_t(x) ≤ 1.
4. Domination of the integrand. For 0 < t ≤ r and every x, |η(u_t(x))| ≤ C·1_{B_r(z)}(x). If x ∈ B_t(z) ⊆ B_r(z), use steps 2–3; otherwise the left side is 0 by step 3. The function C·1_{B_r(z)} is μ-integrable because μ(B_r(z)) < ∞ (integrable_indicator_iff, integrableOn_const). Each x ↦ η(u_t(x)) is continuous, hence AEStronglyMeasurable. So η(u_t(·)) is μ-integrable for every t ∈ (0, r].
5. Proof of (i). For each x, t ↦ η(u_t(x)) is continuous at every t ≠ 0, because u_t(x) = |x − z|²/t² is continuous in t where t² ≠ 0. Apply dominated convergence for parametric integrals (continuousOn_of_dominated on Ioc 0 r) with the bound C·1_{B_r(z)} from step 4, which holds for all t ∈ (0, r]. Hence I is continuous on (0, r].
6. Pointwise derivative. For t ≠ 0 and each x, d/dt (|x − z|²/t²) = −2|x − z|²/t³ = −(2/t)·u_t(x). By the chain rule, t ↦ η(u_t(x)) has derivative F′(t, x) := −(2·u_t(x)·η′(u_t(x)))/t at t.
7. Domination of the derivative. Fix s ∈ (0, r) and let N := (s/2, r). This is an open neighbourhood of s contained in (0, r). Let t ∈ N and x ∈ ℝ^P.
 - If x ∈ B_t(z), then x ∈ B_r(z), and by steps 2–3, |F′(t, x)| = 2·u_t(x)·|η′(u_t(x))|/t ≤ 2M/t ≤ 4M/s.
 - If x ∉ B_t(z), then F′(t, x) = 0 by step 3.
 Hence |F′(t, x)| ≤ (4M/s)·1_{B_r(z)}(x), a μ-integrable bound. Also x ↦ F′(s, x) is continuous, hence AEStronglyMeasurable. Every η(u_t(·)) is AEStronglyMeasurable, and η(u_s(·)) is integrable by step 4.
8. Differentiation under the integral sign. Apply hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le with the neighbourhood N, the bound of step 7 and the pointwise derivatives of step 6 (valid for all t ∈ N, since t ≠ 0 there). So I has derivative ∫ F′(s, x) dμ(x) at s.
9. Formula. ∫ F′(s, x) dμ = ∫ −(2·u_s·η′(u_s))/s dμ = −(∫ 2·u_s·η′(u_s) dμ)/s, by integral_div and integral_neg (identities of Bochner integrals that need no integrability hypothesis). This is the derivative claimed in (ii).
Lean remark (optional aid; the proof above is complete without it): during decomposition, a warning-free, kernel-checked proof of exactly this frozen type was written. It uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and it follows steps 1–9. Scratch copies, which may no longer exist: /tmp/dsmc-em-decomp/C2.lean, and /tmp/dsmc-em-decomp/Full.lean (all four children plus the parent assembly).
proof_key_steps: η′ = deriv η is continuous and vanishes on [1, ∞); |η| ≤ C and |η′| ≤ M on [0, 1].
For t ∈ (0, r] the integrand vanishes off B_t(z) ⊆ B_r(z) and is dominated by C·1_{B_r(z)}, which is integrable since μ(B_r(z)) < ∞; continuity of I on (0, r] follows by continuousOn_of_dominated.
∂_t η(|x − z|²/t²) = −2u_tη′(u_t)/t, dominated by (4M/s)·1_{B_r(z)} for t ∈ (s/2, r).

audit.reason: All hypotheses and the derivative formula match. C¹ regularity makes η′ vanish also at 1, so both integrands vanish outside the open ball. The stated integrable bounds establish continuity through r and differentiation near each interior s for arbitrary μ with finite open-ball mass. No additional measurability or finiteness assumption is hidden.

subproblem.title: Monotonicity of e^{κs}s^{−n}I(s) on (0, r] from the differential inequality nI − sI′ ≤ κsI
subproblem.statement: Let n ∈ ℕ, κ, r ∈ ℝ and I, I′ : ℝ → ℝ. Assume that I is continuous on (0, r], that I has derivative I′(s) at every s ∈ (0, r), and that n·I(s) − s·I′(s) ≤ κ·s·I(s) for every s ∈ (0, r). Then s ↦ e^{κs}·s^{−n}·I(s) (in Lean: fun s => Real.exp (κ * s) / s ^ n * I s) is nondecreasing on (0, r] (MonotoneOn on Ioc 0 r); i.e. e^{κσ}σ^{−n}I(σ) ≤ e^{κρ}ρ^{−n}I(ρ) whenever 0 < σ ≤ ρ ≤ r. No sign condition on κ or on I is assumed; for r ≤ 0 the statement is vacuous.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n : ℕ) (κ r : ℝ) (I I' : ℝ → ℝ), ContinuousOn I (Ioc 0 r) → (∀ s ∈ Ioo 0 r, HasDerivAt I (I' s) s) → (∀ s ∈ Ioo 0 r, (n : ℝ) * I s - s * I' s ≤ κ * s * I s) → MonotoneOn (fun s => Real.exp (κ * s) / s ^ n * I s) (Ioc 0 r)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 4, 3.16–3.17: multiply by the integrating factor and integrate), isolated as a one-variable calculus lemma.
1. Reduction. For s > 0, exp(n·log s) = (exp(log s))^n = s^n, hence exp(κs − n·log s) = e^{κs}/s^n (Real.exp_sub, Real.exp_nat_mul, Real.exp_log). Define G(s) := exp(κs − n·log s)·I(s). Then G(s) = e^{κs}/s^n·I(s) for every s ∈ (0, r]. So it suffices to prove that G is monotone on (0, r] and transfer this along the equality on (0, r] (MonotoneOn.congr).
2. Derivative of G. Let s ∈ (0, r). Since s ≠ 0, log has derivative 1/s at s, so s ↦ κs − n·log s has derivative κ − n/s at s. By the chain rule for exp and the product rule with HasDerivAt I (I′ s) s, G has derivative G′(s) = exp(κs − n·log s)·((κ − n/s)·I(s) + I′(s)) at s.
3. Sign of G′. For s ∈ (0, r), (κ − n/s)·I(s) + I′(s) = (κ·s·I(s) − (n·I(s) − s·I′(s)))/s. The numerator is ≥ 0 by hypothesis and s > 0, so this quotient is ≥ 0. Since exp(·) > 0, G′(s) ≥ 0.
4. Continuity of G on (0, r]. On (0, r] ⊆ (0, ∞), log is continuous, so s ↦ κs − n·log s and its exponential are continuous there. I is continuous on (0, r] by hypothesis, so G is continuous on (0, r].
5. Mean value theorem. The set (0, r] = Ioc 0 r is convex and its interior is (0, r) (interior_Ioc). By steps 2–4, G is continuous on (0, r] and differentiable on (0, r), with deriv G(s) = G′(s) ≥ 0 for s ∈ (0, r). Hence monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg shows that G is monotone on (0, r]. If r ≤ 0, the set is empty and the argument holds trivially.
6. Conclusion. By step 1, s ↦ e^{κs}/s^n·I(s) agrees with G on (0, r], so it is monotone on (0, r].
Lean remark (optional aid; the proof above is complete without it): during decomposition, a warning-free, kernel-checked proof of exactly this frozen type was written. It uses only the axioms propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound, and it follows steps 1–6. Scratch copies, which may no longer exist: /tmp/dsmc-em-decomp/C1.lean, and /tmp/dsmc-em-decomp/Full.lean (all four children plus the parent assembly).
proof_key_steps: On (0, r], e^{κs}/s^n·I(s) = G(s) := exp(κs − n·log s)·I(s).
G′(s) = exp(κs − n·log s)·((κ − n/s)I(s) + I′(s)) for s ∈ (0, r).
(κ − n/s)I + I′ = (κsI − (nI − sI′))/s ≥ 0 by the hypothesis, so G′ ≥ 0 on (0, r).
G is continuous on (0, r]; monotoneOn_of_deriv_nonneg on the convex set Ioc 0 r, whose interior is Ioo 0 r, gives monotonicity; transfer to e^{κs}/s^n·I(s).

audit.reason: The prose and Lean type agree. The logarithmic integrating factor gives the stated nonnegative derivative without sign assumptions on κ or I. Continuity on Ioc and differentiation on its interior justify endpoint monotonicity; nonpositive r is vacuous. The proof is complete and independent.
